officialTitle: Adjuvant Capecitabine for Breast Cancer after Preoperative Chemotherapy
subtypes: Residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: We randomly assigned 910 patients with HER2-negative residual invasive breast cancer after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (containing anthracycline, taxane, or both) to receive standard postsurgical treatment either with capecitabine or without (control).
design.notes: Terminated early after the prespecified interim analysis met the primary endpoint.

sponsor: Advanced Clinical Research Organization / Japan Breast Cancer Research Group
clinicalQuestion: In HER2-negative breast cancer with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, does adjuvant capecitabine improve disease-free and overall survival?

pico.population: HER2-negative breast cancer with residual invasive carcinoma after anthracycline- and/or taxane-containing neoadjuvant chemotherapy

publications.title: Adjuvant Capecitabine for Breast Cancer after Preoperative Chemotherapy.
publications.label: Final analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: The final analysis showed that disease-free survival was longer in the capecitabine group than in the control group (74.1% vs. 67.6% of the patients were alive and free from recurrence or second cancer at 5 years; hazard ratio for recurrence, second cancer, or death, 0.70; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.53 to 0.92; P=0.01).
Overall survival was longer in the capecitabine group than in the control group (89.2% vs. 83.6% of the patients were alive at 5 years; hazard ratio for death, 0.59; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.90; P=0.01).

Among patients with triple-negative disease, the rate of disease-free survival was 69.8% in the capecitabine group versus 56.1% in the control group (hazard ratio for recurrence, second cancer, or death, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.87), and the overall survival rate was 78.8% versus 70.3% (hazard ratio for death, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.30 to 0.90).

Among patients with triple-negative disease, the rate of disease-free survival was 69.8% in the capecitabine group versus 56.1% in the control group (hazard ratio for recurrence, second cancer, or death, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.39 to 0.87), and the overall survival rate was 78.8% versus 70.3% (hazard ratio for death, 0.52; 95% CI, 0.30 to 0.90).

safety.sourceQuote: The hand-foot syndrome, the most common adverse reaction to capecitabine, occurred in 73.4% of the patients in the capecitabine group.

strengths: Randomised phase 3 trial with both DFS and OS benefit
limitations: Open-label; conducted in Japan and Korea, which may affect generalisability
Triple-negative benefit derived from a subgroup analysis; HR+ patients received concurrent endocrine therapy

clinicalImplications.text: Supports adjuvant capecitabine for HER2-negative breast cancer with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, with the greatest apparent benefit in the triple-negative subgroup.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy in TNBC is a trigger for escalation — capecitabine (CREATE-X) is one option, alongside olaparib for germline BRCA carriers (OlympiA).

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 28564564.
